text:
The officer on the screen is wearing an unmarked pressure suit. Your transponder record appears beside a damage report.

"$entity.catchrelease_harpoonHitmanVictim. $entity.catchrelease_harpoonHitmanOrigin. You hit them with $entity.catchrelease_harpoonHitmanOffence."

The officer waits while your comms officer verifies the record.

"They've paid us to deal with you. Anything you'd like to say before we start?"

The officer on the screen is wearing an unmarked pressure suit. Your transponder record appears beside a damage report.

"You hit $entity.catchrelease_harpoonHitmanVictim with $entity.catchrelease_harpoonHitmanOffence in $entity.catchrelease_harpoonHitmanOrigin. They hired us."

Your comms officer points out that the client is no longer around to collect.

"Payment cleared before that happened. We still have a contract."

The officer checks a clause in the contract.

"Cancellation, damages, legal fees. $entity.catchrelease_harpoonHitmanBribeDGS credits, paid now. We both walk away."

The transfer clears. The officer closes your file.

"Contract cancelled. Try not to harpoon someone important, next time."

Your call reaches a damage-control compartment. Someone reads out your transponder code.

"Is this yours?"

An image of the recovered harpoon head appears. Your comms officer confirms that it is fishing equipment.

"Yes, we'd worked that out. What were you trying to catch?"

"Hegemony Navy. $PersonRank $personName."

An incident report appears on your display.

"We've recovered your projectile. Naval Intelligence will examine it. You can apply for a receipt at a military office; quote the number on that report."

$HeOrShe looks up.

"That isn't an invitation to come and collect it."

$PersonRank $personName has an invoice open.

"Repairs, operating time, removal and disposal. Legal is still deciding how to classify the projectile, but I don't expect that to reduce the amount."

The invoice closes.

"They'll contact you."
$PersonRank $personName looks at the damage feed. Then at you. "Whatever purpose that machine was built for, captain, this was not it."

The speaker has the recovered ROD head on the table behind them.

"Accident?" They jab a finger toward it. "You cast Moloch's iron through a ship full of Ludd's children and call it an accident?"

Someone off-screen shouts assent.

"Fire another. See what answer you get."

$personName turns the recovered projectile toward the camera. "You hooked us."

The pirate grins despite everything. "Actually hooked us." Then the grin goes away. "Don't do it again."

"You fired on a vessel of the Sindrian Diktat."

$PersonRank $personName checks the incident record.

"I am required to establish whether the act was deliberate. For your sake, I have entered it as an accident. Do not give me cause to amend that finding."

$PersonRank $personName is searching through a set of regulations.

"Negligent discharge, damage to an associated hull... there's a recovery-equipment provision somewhere."

$HeOrShe gives up looking.

"I will find the appropriate charge, captain. Don't mistake a gap in the index for permission."
"You put a hole in us with fishing gear." $personName rubs the bridge of $hisOrHer nose. "I have to explain that sentence to a yardmaster."

text:
"We've received a damage claim against your fleet."

$PersonRank $personName sends the report, with an image of the recovered harpoon head attached.

"$entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits. Pay the repair and we'll record it as negligent discharge."

$HeOrShe looks at the image again. "Keep that thing pointed away from traffic."

"Cut your drive, captain. We're following up a weapons-discharge report."

$PersonRank $personName sends the assessed damages.

"$entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits. You may settle it now as an accident. A further incident will be treated as a deliberate attack."

"Tri-Tachyon property was damaged by your fleet. The repair assessment is complete."

$PersonRank $personName sends the invoice.

"$entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits, including recovery costs and lost operating time. Pay now and we can close the claim."

"Peace be with you. Cut your drive."

$PersonRank $personName looks at the damage report.

"You damaged a crewed vessel with equipment no prudent captain should point at one."

"The repair is $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits."

"Pay the people whose hull you opened."

"You put Moloch's iron through a ship full of people and now you want this treated as an accident?"

The claim figure appears.

"$entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits. Pay it."

A finger jabs at the recovered-hardware image.

"Then throw that thing out an airlock."

"Hold up." $PersonName grins. "Word says you put a fishing harpoon through somebody's plating."

The grin broadens. "Very funny story. Expensive story. $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS and we're even."

"You have damaged a vessel under Sindrian protection."

$PersonRank $personName sends a penalty notice.

"The State is prepared to accept $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits in settlement. This is a courtesy, captain. A second discharge will not receive the same consideration."

"Damage to an associated hull through negligent operation of heavy recovery equipment."

$PersonRank $personName checks the wording against a regulation.

"$entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits. I appreciate that the equipment was intended for fishing. That does not alter the condition of the other ship."

"Ease off, captain. Someone you harpooned has filed a claim."

$personName sends the yard estimate.

"$entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits. I'm sure you've got an explanation, but they've still got a hole in the hull. Can we settle it?"

"We accepted your explanation the first time."

$PersonRank $personName closes the incident file.

"You're not paying your way out of this one."

The other ships begin spreading into combat formation.

$PersonRank $personName opens the channel just long enough to confirm your identity.

"Yes. That fleet."

The link closes as the other ships move to engage.
"The first incident may have been an accident. The second is deliberate." $PersonRank $personName sets the slate face down. "Weapons are authorized."
"You've done it twice. That does simplify things. Your fleet is now recorded as deliberately hostile to Tri-Tachyon assets. I expect the consequences will be considerably less routine."
$PersonRank $personName does not offer peace this time. "We took payment for the hull and said nothing about the gear that made the hole. That was a courtesy, and you have shown us what it bought."

There is no greeting. The speaker is already shouting when the channel opens.

"Again! Moloch puts a hook in your hand and you cast it into Ludd's children twice?"

Spittle marks the inside of the visor.

"Break the launcher or burn with it."
"Told you what was happening if you did it twice." The pirate stops to think about it. "I didn't, actually. My mistake."
"You were told the penalty was the favourable outcome." $PersonRank $personName closes the notice.

text:
"Captain. Have you got the order?"

The provisioner finds your entry among a list of deliveries and leaves the channel open.

text:
"You supply catch? I've got kitchens asking for more than my usual boats can bring in. I need someone who'll take an order and fill it."

The provisioner shows you the outstanding request. "I'm after $catchreleaseAsk. $catchreleaseDeadline I can offer $catchreleaseReward when you deliver the lot."

text: "Good. I'll put you down for it. Contact me when you've got the full order aboard."
"All right. If you hear of anyone looking for the work, send them my way." The provisioner returns to the supplier list.
"The order's still $catchreleaseAsk. $catchreleaseDeadlineLeft I need the full lot before I can settle up."
The provisioner has the containers checked against the order before arranging your payment. "That's the lot. Good. I'll let the kitchens know they can stop calling me."

The chef answers from a kitchen doorway, with somebody behind $himOrHer trying to ask a question.

"Not now. I'm talking to the supplier." $HeOrShe turns back to the pickup. "Captain. What have you got for me?"
A cook in stained whites is trying to order ingredients over the comm. The supplier has apparently suggested changing the dish. The cook's reply makes several nearby patrons look up.

options: catchrelease_chef_ask:Talk to the cook with the ingredient cards

text:
"Can you get me catch? I'm putting $catchreleaseDish on the menu, and the people who assured me they could supply it have suddenly become difficult to reach."

The chef shows you the ingredient list. "I need all three types: $catchreleaseAsk. $catchreleaseDeadline Bring the complete order to my kitchen and I'll pay $catchreleaseReward."
options:
catchrelease_chef_dish:Why not change the dish?
catchrelease_jobAccept:Take the order.
catchrelease_jobDecline:Decline.

text: "Good. Keep the handling tags on the containers. If my prep crew have to guess which is which, I'll have to start this conversation again."
The chef looks back at the ingredient list. "Fine. Do you know anyone who can?" When you cannot offer a name, $heOrShe starts another call.
"$catchreleaseAskCap. I need all three types. $catchreleaseDeadlineLeft Please don't arrive with two of them and ask whether I can make do."

The chef checks the handling tags, opens one container, and calls for the prep crew.

"Yes. That's what I asked for." $HeOrShe catches an assistant by the sleeve. "Separate stations. I don't want any of this mixed up."

Nobody moves quickly enough.

"Move! I've got the fish, you've got no excuses!"

"Captain! Come in. I've been working on the figures."

The factor opens your current order. There are several versions of the business case behind it, each with a higher sales estimate.
A young factor has reserved the seat opposite with an expensive sleeveless jacket. A ten-page business case is open on $hisOrHer slate; the drink beside it has barely been touched.

options: catchrelease_startup_ask:Hear the pitch from the young factor in the expensive jacket

text:
"Captain. Excellent. I was hoping to speak to someone who actually moves goods."

The factor clears the jacket off the seat and turns the slate toward you. "Fresh catch. Kitchens, private buyers, conservatories. People are already spending money on it, but nobody's bringing those customers together. I have a proposal for doing exactly that."

You ask who will supply the catch.

"That's what I wanted to discuss."

"Restaurants, clubs, private collections. I've worked from population figures and prevailing prices, so this isn't just enthusiasm."

The factor shows you a sales projection. "These are conservative estimates. I've assumed most people won't buy anything."
options:
catchrelease_startup_estimates:That still leaves quite a few who will.
catchrelease_startup_customers:Have any of them agreed to buy?
catchrelease_startup_back:Go over the rest of the proposal.

text:
"You'll deliver to me. I handle the customer side."

You ask where the catch goes after that. The factor opens a diagram linking storage, transport and buyers. None of the companies providing those services is named.

"I'm comparing arrangements. I need an actual consignment before anyone will give me a useful price."
options:

catchrelease_startup_back:Go over the rest of the proposal.

text:
"Three shipments, each larger than the last. I'll pay you for each one when it arrives. No deadline; I need a supplier I can build around, not somebody rushing an unsuitable consignment through."

The first order is for $catchreleaseAsk, with $catchreleaseReward on delivery. The later quantities will follow automatically as each shipment is completed.

"One species per shipment. We can change species between runs. What matters is showing that we can increase the volume."

"Excellent. I'll put you in the business case as a confirmed supplier."

The order arrives before you have left the table. Your quantity and payment are on the first page. There are nine more.

"Of course. You have your own commitments. I appreciate you taking the meeting."

The factor puts the jacket back on the empty seat and starts looking through the bar for another captain.

"We're on $catchreleaseAsk. The current shipment."

The factor checks the order. "No deadline, as agreed. I'd just like to know when I can start describing the stock as available."
The factor checks the delivery against the order and arranges the agreed payment. "Excellent. I'll get this into the figures."

A storage clerk is explaining that charges start when the catch arrives, not when the factor sells it. The factor finds this an unnecessarily narrow way to look at the arrangement.

Your payment clears without difficulty. "First shipment completed. Good. Now we have something to show the buyers."

The next order arrives: $catchreleaseAsk, for $catchreleaseReward on delivery.

"We've had inquiries," the factor tells you while arranging payment. "Several buyers want individual deliveries. The carrier quotes per destination, which makes the first figures look rather severe."

$HeOrShe opens the final order. "Once we're doing enough volume, that should become negligible."

The last shipment is for $catchreleaseAsk. The offered payment is $catchreleaseReward.

The factor puts all three delivery receipts beside the business case and arranges your final payment.

"Three shipments. Increasing volume, all delivered. That's the supply question settled."

You ask whether any of the prospective buyers have placed an order.

"We're discussing quantities. I can have a much more useful conversation with them now." The factor starts updating the projections. "Thank you, Captain. This gives me something real to work with."

The under-butler answers promptly. "Captain. Is this about the specimen?"

$HeOrShe finds your commission in the household schedule. "I'm ready to arrange receipt when you have it."
A $manOrWoman in an immaculately cut coat sits beside an untouched drink. When a server tries to clear the second place, $heOrShe quietly asks that it be left.

text:
The $manOrWoman rises as you approach. "Captain. Thank you for coming. I make purchases for a private household, and I understand that you can procure live specimens."

$HeOrShe waits until you have taken the offered seat. "I have been asked to find one of a particular size. The requirement is quite definite; the species is not."

"The chief butler. It is for his own rooms."

The under-butler appears to anticipate a further question. "I attend to his appointments and personal purchases. The household is a large one."

"A display in his receiving room. The tank has been installed, and he has asked for something that will be visible from the far end."

The under-butler shows you a photograph of the room. "We are not choosing for the kitchen. I mention that because the last supplier misunderstood the request."

text:
"You're a captain, aren't you?" The louder child pushes an empty bucket off the spare chair. "We need someone to get two fish."

"Because you don't know either of us," the quiet child says. "So you won't just give your friend the better fish."

The loud child moves the bucket farther out of your way. "You can sit here, if you want."

text:
The Commissioner recognizes you. "$catchreleaseFightNights $catchreleaseFightNightWord supplying the fights, is it? Word gets around."

"Fancy another? We're after $catchreleaseAsk. $catchreleaseDeadline Fee's $catchreleaseReward."

The barkeeper comes over to hear your answer. "Same arrangement. Take the fee or back a fighter once the odds are up."

"You supply both fighters. I measure each against the normal size range for its species, so a big specimen counts for more than a species that just happens to be big."

The Commissioner shows you the calculations in the book. "An even pair starts at thirty-eight percent each. The rest goes to the house. You can keep the supplier's fee or wager it on either fighter. If your fighter loses, the fee is all you lose."

The barkeeper pours another drink.

"House gets whatever's left between the two. It's all written up there."

"Equal pair means thirty-eight each," the Commissioner says. "Leaves twenty-four for the house."

The bottle goes back on the shelf. "And don't hit the glass. We already replaced it once."

From the benches: "Your shift hasn't picked a winner in three fights."

"Four," somebody answers.

The Commissioner writes your name into the supplier book. "Good. $catchreleaseAsk. $catchreleaseDeadline Bring both in together; we'll weigh them, post the odds, and you can decide what to do with your fee."

"Fair enough." The Commissioner reopens the notebook.

The barkeeper calls down the bar, "Still need two for the fight!"

"Still waiting on $catchreleaseAsk, Captain. $catchreleaseDeadlineLeft"

The Commissioner closes the book before somebody at the next table can spill a drink on it.

text: The Last Entry
Holding for catalogue filing

Expedition $entity.catchreleaseFleetExpedition has completed its survey, but one specimen entry remains open. $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName needs the requested specimen to close the entry and file the catalogue without voiding the expedition's survey classification.
The expedition will accept delivery on the following terms.
"This is the survey vessel $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. Registry $entity.catchreleaseFleetRegistry, expedition $entity.catchreleaseFleetExpedition. Do you take specimen commissions?"

"We're finished here, apart from one entry in the catalogue. If I submit it incomplete, the expedition loses its survey classification. If I keep it open, we keep paying berth and holding fees."

The data officer shows you the missing entry. "I'd like to stop being the reason we can't go home. I need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. We can offer $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline"

options:
catchrelease_fqAccept:I'll take the job.
catchrelease_fqAcceptNoPromise:I'll try, but I can't guarantee the catch. (Accept)
catchrelease_fqDecline:Decline.

text:
"Thank you. I'll send the specimen entry and the range references. You'll find us here when you've got it."

The files arrive under expedition $entity.catchreleaseFleetExpedition.

"Then I'll send the request and range references. Call when you have something I can enter in the catalogue."

The officer adds your name to the commission.

"All right. I'll keep trying other vessels."

The officer leaves the catalogue open and ends the call.

"$entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName, registry $entity.catchreleaseFleetRegistry. Yes, the entry's still open. The captain has asked about it twice this watch."

The data officer brings up the request. "We still need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft"

The expedition staff weigh and photograph the specimen while the data officer fills in the final entry. This time the accession field has a name attached before the officer signs it.

"Accepted. I'll submit the catalogue now."

"That's part of the difficulty." The officer sends the sighting record: $entity.catchreleaseFleetEntryDate, $entity.catchreleaseFleetCoordinates, signed $entity.catchreleaseFleetSignature.

"That name isn't in the personnel index. Nobody by that name has served aboard $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName."

You ask who will sign for your specimen.

"I will."

"The catalogue's filed. I've kept the original sighting with the expedition records; the specimen has its own entry."

The data officer forwards the submission receipt. "Thank you, Captain. We can get underway. $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."
The Escrow
Closing out the contract

Recovery vessel $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName is trying to close contract $entity.catchreleaseFleetContract. The original specimen disappeared with its carrier, but the contract allows a replacement. The skipper needs $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk before the outstanding liability grows any further.
The skipper offers the following terms for a replacement.
"Recovery vessel $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. Skipper speaking. I've got a contract I need off my books."

"We took a recovery contract on a missing shipment. The carrier hasn't turned up, but the liability certainly has. We're down for $entity.catchreleaseFleetLiability, and it grows every day the delivery stays open."

The skipper shows you a clause several pages into the contract. "We can supply a replacement. That's our way out. Get me $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk and I'll pay $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline"

options:
0:catchrelease_fqAccept:I'll take the job.
5:catchrelease_fqAcceptNoPromise:I'll try. No promises. (Accept)
10:catchrelease_fqDecline:Decline.
6:catchrelease_fqHaggle:Their exposure is bigger than your offer.

text:
"Good. I'll register you as the outside supplier. These are the relevant pages of $entity.catchreleaseFleetContract."

The skipper sends the extract. "Bring the specimen here. I'll see to the delivery paperwork."

"An attempt's more than we've got lined up."

The skipper sends the order. "Call when you've found it. I'll have the receiving crew ready."
"All right. I've got other calls out. $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."

"The contract's still open. We're liable for $entity.catchreleaseFleetLiability now."

The skipper checks your manifest. "Have you got $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk? $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft"

The skipper checks the specimen against the replacement clause and signs the receipt before letting the deck crew move it.

"Accepted. You've got your copy; I'm sending the other to the client. That should stop the charges."

"The name was withheld when we took the contract. It still is. Their legal department answers quickly enough when there's another charge to add."

The skipper sends the unmasked specification. "They want $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. Supply that and they have to accept the delivery."
"That's done. Liability's stopped and the contract's closed. Thanks for the work, captain. $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."

The skipper works through the settlement allowance. "I can find some more without referring it back. $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline That's the increased offer."

"No. I've already gone as far as I can sign for. If you want to keep negotiating, it goes to Tri-Tachyon Legal."

The skipper closes the amended offer. "We're back to $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. I'm not adding their review fees to what we already owe."
The skipper opens the amendment again. "All right. I can justify it that way. $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline"
The Interment
Holding for interment

Burial convoy $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName needs the first species named in a guild elder's will before the appointed interment. The convoy has no fishing rig and cannot make a port stop without missing the window.
The estate will accept delivery on the following terms.
"Burial convoy $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. Convoy master speaking. We have a time-sensitive request."

"We're taking a guild elder to interment. An old colleague of mine. The will asks for a specimen of the first species they ever landed to go into the casket."

The convoy master sends the relevant passage. "We hadn't made provision for that. There's no fishing rig aboard, and a port call would make us miss the appointed window. We need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. The estate can offer $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline"

text: "Thank you, Captain. I'll send the species record with the will extract. Hail the lead ship when you're ready to transfer it; I'll receive it myself."
"I understand. We'll count on your attempt, and make what preparations we can while you look. The species record and the time allowed are in the request."

"We'll make other arrangements. Thank you for hearing us out."

The convoy master closes the channel.
"$entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName here. We're ready to depart as soon as the casket is complete. Have you found $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk? $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft"

The convoy master meets the container in the hold. It is checked against the will, wrapped and marked with the elder's name.

"That's the right one. Thank you for bringing it."

"First catch goes with them, last catch closes the log. An old guild custom."

The convoy master checks the wording of the will. "It means the species, not the original fish. They were quite specific about that. I wish they'd been as specific about who was to fetch it."
"The casket is complete. We can make the interment window." The convoy master is already checking the departure order. "We're getting underway. Safe passage, captain."
The Calibration Pair
Calibrating instruments

The survey vessel $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName has two instruments giving different readings from the same standards. Its Academy field contract calls for a pair of specimens of the same species before the researcher can finish recalibration and resume the survey.
The Academy field contract offers the following terms.
"Survey vessel $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName, operating under Academy field contract. We require assistance with our equipment."

"Two meters, one certified standard, two results. They agreed before our last transit through worn fabric. Now they don't, and I can't declare either one correct just because I prefer its reading."

The researcher sends the calibration request. "Procedure calls for a specimen pair of the same species: $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. The contract pays $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline"

text: "Good. I'll send the procedure. Please keep the retrieval records with each specimen; I need to be able to tell which result belongs to which catch."

"I'll take an attempt. We've run out of useful things to recalibrate here."

The researcher sends the procedure with your order.
"Very well. I'll ask the next vessel. We have plenty of time to repeat the same unhelpful measurements in the meantime."

"I still need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. One of my assistants has labelled a meter 'probably correct.' I dislike writing 'probably' in a calibration record. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft"

The researcher has both specimens put through the instrument set, then asks for the sequence to be repeated. The second readings are entered beside the first rather than written over them.

"That's the pair delivered. I'll arrange your payment."

"The same certified mass gives a different number on each meter. Repeating the test gives us another pair of numbers."

The researcher shows you the record. "We're keeping all of them. The specimen pair gives us a reference that hasn't spent the last transit bolted into our calibration locker."

"That's enough. I can file the calibration certificate." The researcher signs the final sheet. "If the Academy wants a fourth column, they can issue a new contract. $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."

"One of the specimens returned a different result on its second pass. Your delivery's accepted; this is an additional request."

The researcher opens another column. "Procedure calls for a third specimen of the same species. I need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk, for $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline Would you take that on?"
"Thank you. I'll send the amended request. One more specimen, then I should have enough to file."
"Understood. The first delivery remains accepted and paid. I'll find somebody else for the additional specimen."
"I still have the first pair and an unfinished certificate. We need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk to complete the additional request."

The researcher runs all three specimens through the same sequence, recording the results in separate columns.

"That's enough to complete the procedure. Whether the Academy likes the readings is its own problem."
One reference specimen on $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName returned a different result on its second pass. Procedure requires a third specimen of the same species as a tiebreaker.
The follow-up calibration request has the following terms.
The Mutiny Pot
Holding the buyout
The crew of $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName has pooled shares for three years to buy out its captain. They hired you privately to supply the specimen required by the sale agreement.
The crew's private offer has the following terms.
"Bosun of $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. Requesting a private word on ship's business."

"We've been putting part of every share into a buyout fund. Three years of it. There's finally enough to buy $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName."

The bosun checks that the channel is private before sending the sale agreement. "The captain signed, but there's a condition. We have to bring in the species from an old lost cargo wager. Captain won't sell until it's settled."

"We need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. This stays off the ship's open channels until it's aboard. The crew can offer $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline"

text: "Good. I'll send the sale clause and the old wager entry." The files arrive under the crew's account. "Keep this between us until you hail back."

"All right. I'll tell the crew we've found someone."

The bosun sends the old wager entry. "Hail me when you've got the specimen. Not the bridge."
"Fair. Appreciate the discretion. $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."

"Bosun here. We've got the fund together and the sale papers ready. Everything's waiting on $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk."

The bosun lowers their voice. "Please tell me you've found it. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft"

The bosun compares the container tag with the sale agreement and has a crewman countersign the delivery.

"That's the last condition. The money's ready, and now the fish is aboard. The captain can sign the transfer."

"We've all heard that wager story. Who won, who cheated, what the catch looked like. Depends on the evening."

The bosun shows you the signed clause. "The species in this copy is definite. That's what we're holding the captain to."

"The ship's ours." The bosun is on the bridge now, giving departure instructions. "We'll take $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName into port and get the rest of the paperwork done there."

The bosun comes back to the pickup. "Thank you, Captain. Three years was long enough."

"A captain reads his own manifest. I know about the pot."

The captain takes the bosun's place on the channel. "Bring me $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk privately and I'll pay $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestCounterReward. My account, not theirs."

The sale agreement remains open on the display. "When anyone asks, I landed it. That's part of the arrangement."

text: "Done." The captain sends the wager entry and a private hand-in code. "Bring it to me. Don't route the container through general cargo."

"Then do your business with the bosun."

The channel changes hands. The bosun looks at you for a moment before bringing the crew's offer back up. "Our terms haven't changed."
"Captain here. The purchase papers are still waiting on the last line. I still need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk."

The captain has the container brought through a side lock, away from the general cargo crew. After checking the specimen against the wager entry, the captain signs your private receipt.

"That's our business settled. Leave the sale to me."

"You've been paid, Captain. There's nothing else I need from you."

The captain ends the call. A cargo canister is put out through a lower lock; nobody aboard asks you to collect it.
The captain of $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName knows about the crew's buyout and has made a private counteroffer for the same specimen. They intend to present it as their own catch.
The captain's counteroffer has the following terms.
The Tribute
Finding the tribute

Independent salvage crew $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName owes its yearly tribute to a local pirate ring. The courier sent to fetch the requested specimen never returned, and the ring's enforcers have arrived to collect. The quartermaster needs a replacement before the pirates decide to collect something else.
The quartermaster has offered the following payment for the replacement tribute.
"Independent freighter $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. Quartermaster speaking. If you've got a fishing rig, answer private. Please."

"We've been at this eleven weeks."

The captain sends a species record, followed by an inventory of the fleet's cargo.

"Wrong gear. Wrong places, mostly. A great deal of advice from people who've never caught one either."

"I need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. You bring it here, you get $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. That's what I've got to offer."

The captain closes the inventory.

"$entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline The sooner the better. I'd like to go home."

options:
0:catchrelease_fqAccept:I'll take the job.
5:catchrelease_fqAcceptNoPromise:I'll try. No promises. (Accept)
10:catchrelease_fqDecline:Decline.

text: "Good. I'll send you the record for $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. Bring it here when you have it."

"Nobody's promised me anything useful yet. I'll settle for someone who knows what they're doing."

The order arrives. "I'll keep your payment aside."

"All right."

The captain closes the channel.

"Any luck?"

The captain waits for your answer before bringing up the order.

"Still looking for $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft"

The captain opens the container personally. There is a long inspection, with frequent glances at an old photograph.

"That's it. That'll do."

An order goes out to transfer your payment. The captain is still looking at the specimen when the crew come to take it away.

"It belonged to my old captain. I looked after the collection."

The captain closes the collection record.

"I got into debt. Sold one. Told myself I'd replace it before anyone noticed."

"Now he's retiring. Wants the collection packed up and sent on. Which means someone is going to count it."

The captain looks away from the pickup. "That's what the eleven weeks are for."

"It's packed. I've sent word that the collection's ready."

The captain starts to say something else, then thinks better of it.

"Thank you. I mean it."
Short of Quota
Filling quota

The purser aboard $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName is trying to fill a shortfall on station provisioning contract $entity.catchreleaseFleetContract. An incomplete delivery would let the station reopen the fleet's rates in arbitration. The purser can buy qualifying fish from you out of the season's remaining margin; species can be mixed.
The purser can authorize a supplemental purchase on the following terms.
"Fishing fleet $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName, purser's office. Sorry to trouble you, captain. We're short on a provisioning contract and I understand you've got fishing gear aboard."

The purser takes the call on the working deck. Someone in the background shouts a tally.

"Count it again," the purser calls back, then turns to you. "Sorry, captain. I know what the count is. I'd just rather it weren't."

"We're short $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk on contract $entity.catchreleaseFleetContract. That's a station provisioning order. If we file short, they can send the whole thing to arbitration and start discussing our rates."

"I can buy against the shortfall without asking the owners. $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward is as far as my authority goes."

The grade requirements follow the offer.

"Any species that meets those terms. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline And please check the grade. I've already had enough arguments about what ought to count."

options:
0:catchrelease_fqAccept:I'll take the job.
5:catchrelease_fqAcceptNoPromise:I'll try. No promises. (Accept)
10:catchrelease_fqDecline:Decline.

text:
"Thank you. I'll record you as an outside supplier and send the relevant contract line."

The contract extract and grade record follow. "Please use that grade schedule when you sort the catch. If anything falls outside it, I can't put it against the quota."

"Then I'll open the purchase order in your name. It doesn't oblige you to deliver what you haven't caught, but those are the terms if you do."

The purser sends the grade schedule with the order.
"Yes, understood. Sorry to take your time." The purser's eyes drop to the ledger again. "We'll keep our boats out and see what comes in. $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."

"We brought another boat in. Most of it graded below contract."

The purser turns the ledger toward the pickup.

"Still short $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft"

The purser meets the transfer on the working deck with two tally clerks and the contract grade sheet.
The catch is counted and checked as it comes across.

One specimen is set aside, examined again, then returned to the accepted lot.

"There. That's the quota."

The purser checks the figure once more before signing the receipt.

"Same grounds we've fished for years. Some stopped producing. Some shifted, and now we spend the fuel finding them."

The purser shows you several old returns, all comfortably above the present quota.

"That's what the station will bring to arbitration. They'll ask what's changed aboard our ships. I've got no figure I can put against 'the fish aren't where they used to be.'"

"So I buy what's missing and hope next season is better."

"Filed complete. I've kept a copy of your grade report in case they query it."

For once, the purser closes the ledger.

"Thank you, captain. You've saved us a very unpleasant meeting."
Hungry Fleet
Rationing

After $entity.catchreleaseFleetRationDays days of printed protein, the crew of $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName has submitted a proposed menu to command. The galley chief has been given the job of finding something worth cooking. Any species will do, provided your delivery meets the order.
The galley chief's provisioning offer is recorded on the following terms.
"Galley chief aboard $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. I'm the cook, and command has wisely left this negotiation to me."

"Captain. I understand you fish."

The galley chief has taken over a corner of the mess for the call.

"We've been eating printed protein for $entity.catchreleaseFleetRationDays days. The crew petitioned command this morning. Very respectful. They even attached a menu."

The chief holds it up.

"I've worked in galleys for twenty years. I don't need a gunner explaining stew to me. I need something to put in the pot."

"$entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. Species doesn't matter, so long as it meets the order. I have $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward to spend. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline"

"And if anyone asks, I was arranging this before the petition."

options:
0:catchrelease_fqAccept:I'll take the job.
5:catchrelease_fqAcceptNoPromise:I'll try. No promises. (Accept)
10:catchrelease_fqDecline:Decline.

text: "Good. I'll send the order and receiving instructions. The crew will want to know your name."

"Then I'll count you as our supplier. Sending the order now."

The chief lowers their voice. "I won't announce the menu until it's aboard."
"A pity. I'll keep looking. I'll tell the petition committee you were polite. $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."

"$entity.catchreleaseFleetRationDays days. They've added desserts to the petition."

The chief shows you the new page, then puts it away.

"I still need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft"

The galley chief inspects the delivery container by container before waving each one through to prep. Their shoulders finally come down.

"Good. Cold storage, second rack. Knives out. Somebody get the large pans hot."

The galley erupts into motion.

"No. The printer produces everything a human body needs. Ask the medical officer. Ask the captain. Neither of them has to stand here while it's eaten."

The chief looks across the mess.

"I've started putting out condiments we used to use for cleaning. I'd like to stop."

"Night watch gets the same portions as everyone else. I've had to write that on the door."

Something boils over behind the chief.

"Right. Thank you, captain. If you'll excuse me, I've finally got work to do."

id: # fleet quest: scavenger with a dead engine

text: Scavenger with a Dead Engine
Repacking the drive coil

A drive coil aboard $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName needs repacking, but the scavengers have run out of gel. Their technician found an approved substitute made from rendered fish. Suitable species occur nearby; you don't have to catch them in any particular system.
The repair supply request is recorded on the following terms.
"Coil technician aboard the scavenger $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. We've got a drive repair held up for lack of one consumable."

"We can repair it. We've got the tools, we've got the winding, we've even got someone who knows how. No packing gel."

The coil technician opens a yard manual to section $entity.catchreleaseFleetManualSection.

"This is going to sound stupid. The approved substitute is a compound rendered from fish."

"I've checked the edition. I've checked the correction sheets. It's still there."

"We need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. You can find those around here. The order includes the handling requirements."

"The salvage haul will cover $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline"

options:
0:catchrelease_fqAccept:I'll get what you need.
5:catchrelease_fqAcceptNoPromise:I'll try. No promises. (Accept)
10:catchrelease_fqDecline:Decline.
8:catchrelease_fqQuestion:How does a fish pack a drive coil?

text: "Good. I'll send the manual extract and receiving instructions. Try to believe the manual. I'm trying."

"All right. I'll register the order. Check it against the manual extract before you bring anything over."

The technician sends both files. "I'd rather not dismantle the coil twice."
"Figured. We'll keep looking for another supply. $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."

"Coil condition still reads $entity.catchreleaseFleetCoilCondition. We're leaving it cold until we've repacked it."

The technician retrieves the order. "$entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft"

The specimen is transferred to engineering.
Some time later, the repaired drive comes up to a steady tone.

Conversation on the working deck stops for a few seconds while the crew listens.

A deckhand starts the salvage invoice, reaches the description field and leaves the cursor blinking.

"We render it. Filter the useful fraction, warm it up, pack it around the winding."

The technician traces the procedure with a finger.

"Eighteen to twenty-two percent yield. Good from minus forty to two hundred ten. Then two low-load cycles before we trust it."

"I was hoping you'd say you'd heard of it."

"Holding temperature. No leakage. No fault."

The technician watches the readings for another few seconds.

"I'm putting a copy of that page in the repair locker. Thanks for stopping, captain."
A scavenger vessel is holding position with its drive cold. A standard assistance request is running on the local trade band.
Burn Ward
Treating burn casualties

A reactor-space fire aboard $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName left $entity.catchreleaseFleetCasualties crew badly burned. With the synthskin exhausted, the medical officer needs fish skin for temporary dressings. Only fish caught after you accept the request will be fresh enough for the work.
The medical officer's request is recorded on the following terms.
"Thank you for answering. Medical officer, $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. We had a fire and I have burn casualties."

"Thank you for answering. We had a fire in the reactor space."

The medical officer moves the pickup away from the occupied beds.

"$entity.catchreleaseFleetCasualties casualties. I've used the last of the synthskin. The rest have gel dressings, but I can't keep changing those indefinitely."

"I've used fish skin on burns before. Frontier posting. It can keep the wounds covered until we reach a hospital."

The officer sends a handling note.

"$entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. Caught after you take the job, please. I need to know how long it's been out of the water."

"We can pay $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline I'd be grateful if you came straight back once you have it."

options:
0:catchrelease_fqAccept:I'll bring you the fish.
5:catchrelease_fqAcceptNoPromise:I'll try. No promises. (Accept)
10:catchrelease_fqDecline:Decline.

text:
"Thank you. I'm sending our position and a handling note."

The note is two lines long. Keep the catch cold. Leave the skin on.

"I'll record the request as accepted. I understand you can't promise the catch."

The handling note arrives: keep it cold and leave the skin intact.

"Then we'll keep broadcasting."

The channel closes.

"Still treating them. I'd hoped to have them off the gel by now."

The officer checks the order. "$entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk, caught since you took the job. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft"

A medic meets the transfer with an insulated trolley. The catch goes straight to the medbay, where a team is ready to clean and prepare the skin.

The medical officer checks the capture record, then calls for the first patient to be brought through.

"I've treated miners with it. I'd rather use synthskin, but I don't have any."

The officer finds a treatment record and turns the display toward you.

"That man had burns across most of his back. We got him through the journey and into a hospital. That's what I'm trying to do here."

"All $entity.catchreleaseFleetCasualties have proper dressings now. We're arranging a transfer to a hospital."

The officer pulls off a pair of gloves.

"You've helped. Thank you, captain."
A small trader is broadcasting a distress call with a medical priority code. Scans show fire damage around its reactor section.
Fouled Line
Holding at a fouled breach

Both drones belonging to the fishing boat $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName are stuck beyond $entity.catchreleaseFleetRupture. The skipper is relying on an old remedy: another crew brings aboard a fresh catch from the same rupture. Your catch must come from that rupture after you accept the request.
The skipper's request is recorded on the following terms.
"$entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. We're a fishing crew and we're stuck. You're the first hull that's stopped."

"Both of them. First one stopped coming back, sent the second to find it."

The skipper shows you two drone tracks ending inside $entity.catchreleaseFleetRupture.

"Six hours. They're still answering. I can tell them to return all I like; they don't move."

"Those drones are worth more than the boat. I'd sooner not leave them behind."

A deckhand interrupts to report the coherence reading. The skipper listens, then sends the deckhand away.

"There's something we can try. Another crew fishes the same breach and brings a catch aboard us. I've seen it free a fouled line."

"$entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk, from $entity.catchreleaseFleetRupture after you take the job. We can pay $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline"

options:
0:catchrelease_fqAccept:I'll work the breach.
5:catchrelease_fqAcceptNoPromise:I'll try. No promises. (Accept)
10:catchrelease_fqDecline:Decline.

text:
"Thank you. I'll send the fix and both drone tracks. Give those tracks some room."

The skipper marks them on your chart. "Bring the catch here once you've landed it."

"I'll take the attempt. Putting your name against the job now."

The rupture and drone tracks arrive on your chart. "Anything you bring us has to come out of that breach after this call."

"Right. We'll keep calling."

The channel closes.

"Still answering. Still won't move."

The skipper leaves the tracks on screen.

"We need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk from $entity.catchreleaseFleetRupture. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft"

A deckhand carries your catch aboard in a sealed tank and sets it down on the bridge.
The skipper logs it against $entity.catchreleaseFleetRupture.

A few minutes later, both drone tracks start moving toward the boat.

"Then we leave them."

The skipper looks at the tracks.

"I keep saying they cost more than the boat. Doesn't mean I ought to lose the boat as well."

"Couldn't tell you. My first skipper did it twice. Both times, the drone came home once the other crew's catch was aboard."

"We can have a good laugh about it if it doesn't work. I'd like to try it first."

"Both drones are back in the rack. One lost a sensor mast, but that we can fix."

The skipper is already plotting a course away from the breach. "Burn bright, captain."
A small fishing boat is holding station at a rupture and broadcasting a distress call. It has not moved since the call began.
Collector's Commission
Waiting

A collector aboard $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName has repeatedly lost specimens to last-minute sales through other brokers. Suspecting a rival buyer, the collector has commissioned you directly to supply the missing entry in an otherwise carefully prepared display.
The private commission is recorded on the following terms.
"Private vessel $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. I have a collection commission to place, if you are taking work."

"I have a tank ready. The nameplate was engraved two years ago."

The collector sends you the requirements for the missing specimen.

"$entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. Three brokers have accepted my deposit. Three have returned it just before transfer because the specimen was suddenly unavailable."

"I believe someone else is buying them. Through agents, naturally. Nobody will give me a name."

"So I am approaching someone who can obtain one without a broker. My offer is $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline"

"The receiving instructions are quite precise. I have had time to revise them."

options:
0:catchrelease_fqAccept:I'll take the commission.
5:catchrelease_fqAcceptNoPromise:I'll try. No promises. (Accept)
10:catchrelease_fqDecline:Decline.

text: "Very good. I will transmit the collection entry and receiving requirements."

"An accepted commission, then, with payment on delivery. I would rather you took care over it than made assurances you couldn't keep."

The receiving instructions run to several pages.
"Understood. I will continue the search. $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."

"The holding conditions are ready. I test them every morning."

The collector checks your commission.

"$entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft Please tell me before you transfer it. I wish to be there."

The collector receives the container personally and takes it to the display tank.
They compare the holding temperatures, set the acclimation flow and wait beside the tank until the transfer is complete.

The specimen settles behind the glass beneath the engraved nameplate.

"They are perfectly willing to sell. Right up until it is time to deliver."

The collector shows you three transactions, dated $entity.catchreleaseFleetBrokerDates.

"Carthen & Vale. Morrow Exchange. Silex Acquisitions. Different brokers, almost identical apologies."

"I cannot prove it is the same buyer. I would be very interested to hear another explanation."

"There it is."

The collector watches the tank.

"I should send the brokers a photograph. No. No, I don't think I will."

"Thank you, captain. It is exactly what I wanted."

The collector turns the pickup toward an empty display tank. The lighting is on, the filters are running, and a nameplate is already fixed beneath the glass.

"For that."

After a moment, the collector adds, "Eighteen point five degrees. A ten-hour display cycle. I think it will do very well."
Settling a Bet
Arguing

Two watches aboard $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName have turned a disagreement over survey returns into a substantial bet. Their captain wants a pair of matching specimens to compare with the records and put an end to it. The fish must be the same species and meet the wager's other terms.
The wager has the following terms.

"Scavenger fleet $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. Captain speaking. I've got an argument between two watches that's gone on long enough. They put money on it, naturally.
If you fish, you might be able to settle it for us."

"It started with a bottle."

The captain sends two survey logs from the same fishing ground.

"First watch reckons these returns prove there's a run. Second watch reckons they got lucky twice and wrote a report about it."

"Now there's money involved. Enough that I don't want to settle it by telling them both to shut up."

"I need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. Two of the same species, so we can compare them with the returns. The pot will cover $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadline"

"I've forbidden any more betting. That hasn't improved the atmosphere."

options:
0:catchrelease_fqAccept:I'll take the job.
5:catchrelease_fqAcceptNoPromise:I'll try. No promises. (Accept)
10:catchrelease_fqDecline:Decline.

script:
# the label needs a colon, which the Options column cannot hold
SetOptionText catchrelease_fqExtraQuestion "For the record: which side am I proving?"

text:
"Good. I'll send the logs with the order."

The captain pauses to address someone off-screen. "No, hiring someone doesn't void it. We agreed on outside verification."

"An attempt is enough to get them waiting for a result. I'll put you down for it."

The logs and the accepted order arrive together.
"All right. I'll deal with them. $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."

"They've started disputing the terms of the bet. We wrote them down. That hasn't helped."

The captain brings up your order. "$entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeadlineLeft"

A couple of crew from each watch come forward to inspect the catch.

There is some muttering before the captain cuts them off and checks the specimens against the logs. "That's enough. Pay out the bets."

The captain authorizes the transfer to your account.

"First watch says repeated returns mean the species is established there. Second watch says the returns don't prove what they caught."

The captain points out the disputed readings.

"They've both explained it to me several times. We need actual specimens to compare with this before I have to hear it again."

"Paid out. Both watches signed for it."

Someone speaks off-screen.

"No, we're not taking bets on whether the sample was representative."

The captain turns back. "Thank you, captain. I'll handle the rest."

"Neither. You're bringing the specimens. We compare them with the logs and settle it here."

"The fee is the same whichever watch wins. I insisted on that before calling you."

Your sensors officer finds an old auxiliary in the debris. Most of its useful fittings have been stripped, but a large servicing frame remains clamped to the dorsal deck.

The frame has its own maneuvering thrusters and a dead transponder. Its docking points could take something nearly the size of a fighter.

The boarding party finds a cold reactor, empty lockers and a galley nobody thought worth stripping. There are no bodies.

Your ops chief sends an image of the external frame.

"LYNE markings. Looks like rig-servicing equipment. Some of these codes aren't in our registry."

Someone has scratched maintenance intervals into the casing by hand. The most recent entry is worn almost smooth.

The crew can recover the assembly intact, although the cargo chief has some complaints about the clamps.

text:
Your comms officer picks up a personal beacon running on emergency power. It leads to a prefabricated surface cache.

Someone has made a living compartment out of one of the storage bays. Its occupant is thin, dirty, and already waving at the camera.

A garbled transmission calls out almost immediately.

"You came back! Please take me aboard, $PlayerSirOrMadam, I beg of you!"

options: 30:catchrelease_ratingMurder:Order a cannon fired at the beacon

text:
"Missed the boat."

He sees your expression and hurries on.

"We were doing a transfer. Skipper thought I was on the tender. Tender thought I was back aboard. Both had the same manifest, so both signed and left."

He gestures at the compartment behind him.

"I waited for them to notice. Then I thought I'd better see what was in the cache."

script:

text:
"Fishing crew. Worked with the Fisherman's boats."

He digs out an old comm unit and reads your officer a fleet handshake.

"Try that when you find them. Trawlers, usually, out past the settled traffic. Tell the Fisherman who you've got aboard. He'll know me."

You order bombardment of the coordinates the beacon is broadcasting from. 

It falls silent with a single shot.

He accepts before you finish the sentence.

Your personnel officer finds a spare berth.

The Fisherman answers from a worktable. He puts down a dismantled control unit and wipes his hands before taking the call.

"Evening, Captain. What can I do for you?"

"Captain. Back with a catch?"

A crewman passes behind the Fisherman carrying a sealed crate. By the time he reaches the hatch his hands are empty. The Fisherman waits while your comms officer clears the channel.

"Evening." The Fisherman's voice comes through before the comm indicator turns green. When the picture arrives, he is pouring a drink into a battered mug.

"Go ahead. I'm listening."

The Fisherman is watching someone work out of view when the link opens. "Easy with that. Set it down first."

Metal strikes a deck plate on your left audio channel, though the trawler lies to starboard. He turns back to the pickup. "Sorry, Captain. You were saying?"

text:
"I'd have a look at $catchreleaseRumorSystem if you're after something scarce. I've had catches in from there that I wouldn't normally expect to see on the same manifest."

The Fisherman sends you the report. "The rarer patterns are coming through more often. Worth a trip while it lasts."

"$catchreleaseRumorSystem has been bringing up a fair amount of bycatch. Crews are finding more of it during retrieval, though most of the tally is ordinary salvage."

He sends the recent returns across. "Leave yourself some hold space if you're going."

"Have you been looking for $catchreleaseRumorStranger? There are catches coming in from $catchreleaseRumorSystem, outside its usual range."

The Fisherman attaches the report. "The specimens have been good, too. I wouldn't alter the permanent chart on the strength of it, but I'd fish there now."

"There's been some heavy catch coming out of $catchreleaseRumorSystem. Enough of it that the buyers have started asking where the boats worked."

He sends you the measurements. "Nothing outside the usual limits. You're just more likely to land a big one at the moment."

"Try $catchreleaseRumorSystem if you want an easier retrieval. The fish haven't been running as hard there lately."

The Fisherman checks the date on the report before sending it. "You still have to follow them, but it should give you a bit more time to correct a mistake."

"$catchreleaseRumorSystem is worth a look for salvage. Some of the bycatch coming up there has been valuable enough to pay for the trip."

He opens the tally for you. "Not more chances to grab it, necessarily. Better odds that what you get is worth keeping."

"There's a good report from $catchreleaseRumorSystem. Rarer patterns are turning up often enough that I'd go after them now."

He includes the salvage tally with the catch records. "The crews working there have been seeing more bycatch during retrieval as well. You may come home with more than the fish you went for."

"I'd try $catchreleaseRumorSystem. The catches have been heavier than usual, and the retrievals are easier."

The Fisherman reads a little further down the report. "Good place to fill an order for a large specimen. Less work chasing it around once you've got hold."

"$catchreleaseRumorStranger has been turning up in $catchreleaseRumorSystem. It's outside the charted range, but the catches are there."

He passes you the retrieval records as well. "They've had an easier time landing fish in that system lately. If you're missing this one, now would be a good time to try."

"Keep some room in the hold if you go to $catchreleaseRumorSystem. Crews there have been seeing more bycatch during retrieval, and a fair share of it has been worth selling."

He sends the tally. "There's scrap in there too. Don't throw away a good catch chasing every bit of it."

"$catchreleaseRumorSystem is holding remarkably well. Much better than it usually does."

The Fisherman sends you the latest coherence report. "If you've been avoiding it because of the fabric, you might want to take the opportunity. Don't expect the change to be permanent."

"Check this before you go through $catchreleaseRumorSystem. The fabric's barely holding, and that isn't what the usual chart will tell you."

The Fisherman leaves the coherence report open. "You can still fish it. Keep the trip short, and don't leave your crew sitting there while you decide what else to catch."
"Nothing worth sending you after."

text:
"Bycatch. The rig brings other things through with the pattern. Wreckage, cargo, sometimes something you can use."

The Fisherman looks over your salvage manifest. "The LYNE's clamps limit what you can recover. There are modifications for heavier loads; ask around in port for the schematics if you mean to make a habit of it."

options: catchrelease_ask_howLong:How long have you been out here?

text:
"I was working with the ROD when it was still a cargo-handling project. There wasn't much interest in fishing at the time."

The Fisherman checks the control unit in front of him. "We've changed the equipment a fair bit since then."

options: catchrelease_ask_whyOut:Why are you always so far out?

text:
"Fabric's thick where people are. A settled world, a station, all that living in one place: it helps things hold."

He brings up the local chart. "Out here there's less of it. Easier to open a rupture, and you can work without putting a traffic lane through the middle of your fishing."

options: catchrelease_ask_looking:What happens to somebody who looks at the catch?

text: "They look." He turns a control unit over in his hands. "Don't mistake it for seeing you."

"Enough of one that I wouldn't start treating the catch as a passenger."

The Fisherman puts the control unit down. "You can watch what it does, Captain. Be careful what you decide that means."

options: catchrelease_ask_patterns:The patterns. What are they, actually?

text:
"Pattern is the technical term for what takes shape as we bring it through. You'll find it in the retrieval records. Ghost is the older spacer name."

The Fisherman brings up a catch entry. "When you're selling it, fish will usually do. The buyer can see what you've brought."

"That isn't something the range record will tell you. It will tell you where to find one and what you'll need to bring it home."

He leaves the catch entry on the display. "Start there."

options: catchrelease_ask_deepWater:Why is the deep water worse?

text: "Not water. Thinner fabric. A pattern gets less help holding one shape out there. Same goes for your crew. Keep the trip short, and don't turn it into research."

options: catchrelease_ask_searchlightDrones:Why can't I use the drones with the searchlights?

text:
"The lights don't open a full breach. You can reach a pattern with a ROD, but an ordinary drone can't make the trip back. You'd be leaving it stuck beyond the fabric."

The Fisherman opens the harpoon schematic. "The harpoon's return trace stays connected to the ship. It doesn't have to find its own way across."

text:
"Work? If you're taking a ship out past the picket, try the fishing boats."

The spacer turns the glass between both hands.

"They're usually holding away from the inhabited traffic. Big rigs. Need a crane for half the servicing."

"Ask for the Fisherman. He'll find something for you if you're willing."

"That's what they call it."

The spacer considers the objection. "There's catch. There's buyers. There's gear. Sounds like fishing from my end of the loading bay."

"Out past the settled orbits. They don't come in to berth much."

"Look for trawlers. If there's one in-system, hail it and ask. Someone will know where he is."

text:
"Terrible!" He seems delighted. "Crablobab. Me and the crabs. Saves introductions."

A claw emerges from the crate. He takes it between two fingers and pushes it back in through the opposite side.

"You fish. Good! I've been waiting for a customer with problems."

He opens his coat a little. "Or money. Either is a promising start."

text:
"You!" Crablobab points with both hands. "$catchreleaseCrabExplosiveTarget!"

Something flashes inside his shoulder pocket.

"So it worked! Come, tell me all about it. Was it loud? Of course it was loud. I put that in myself."

He makes room on the counter. "You'll be wanting another."

"Back again! Excellent. A returning customer."

He retrieves a crab from the next stool and puts it through a pocket into the crate.

"That one too. Very good for business, all this coming back. What have you run out of?"

"Dependable! Easy to count. If you lose one, look under something."

He pats the crate. Something inside his coat knocks back.

"And everybody wants crabs. You do, for instance. You came straight over."

Crablobab opens his coat. The shelves are empty.

He checks one pocket, then another. A crab checks the first one again.

"Nothing." He considers this. "Except crabs."

Crablobab opens his coat. The inside contains shelves. One of them is far enough away to require a light.

"Shop!"

Crablobab reaches past a shelf several metres inside his coat and retrieves a cartridge box.

"Celebration charges! They go off when the catch comes aboard. Paper, colours, everybody looks up. Much better than telling the crew you've caught something."

He gives the box a shake.

"You'll be finding paper in the vents for weeks. A lasting impression!"

The price is $catchreleaseCrabCelebrationPrice and $catchreleaseCrabCelebrationCrabs crabs.

"Celebration charges! Catch comes aboard, these go off. Paper everywhere. Even the engine room gets some eventually."

Crablobab takes a cartridge box from a high shelf inside his coat.

"$catchreleaseCrabCelebrationPrice and $catchreleaseCrabCelebrationCrabs crabs."

He considers what you have, then sets the box aside.

"Not quite. We'll celebrate when you've got the rest!"

He hands you a box too large for the breast pocket it came out of.

"The Outfitter can switch them on and off. Very important, the off. People ask for it after the first few catches."

Crablobab brushes a strip of coloured paper from your shoulder.

"Whispering? These!"

Crablobab already has a pair of earmuffs in his hands. He presses the cushions together for your inspection.

"Comfortable. Good seal. Put them on and you don't have to listen anymore."

He lays them beside a little recorder taken from his coat. Faint whispering comes from its speaker.

"$catchreleaseCrabEarmuffsPrice, and $catchreleaseCrabEarmuffsCrabs crabs. For the pair. People always ask."

"Whispering? These!"

Crablobab presses the cushions of a pair of earmuffs together.

"Comfortable. Good seal. Put them on and you don't have to listen anymore. $catchreleaseCrabEarmuffsPrice, and $catchreleaseCrabEarmuffsCrabs crabs."

He counts what you can offer, then draws the earmuffs into his sleeve.

"Almost! But I can't sell you just the one. The other ear would complain."

"Try them."

The cushions are warm. Once fitted, you can no longer hear the whispering from the recorder.

"There. Much nicer. The Outfitter will keep the setting for you."

Crablobab continues talking while you take them off. He appears to have been recommending them the entire time.

"Chicken!"

Crablobab produces a display tile from behind a rack of boxed merchandise inside his coat. A chicken crosses the screen, disappears off one edge and comes back at the other.

"For the fishing display. When you haven't got a head that shows the fish on the hook, he stands in. See? Already at work."

He turns the tile to give you a better view. The chicken turns with it.

"Doesn't tell you what you've hooked. He's a chicken. But you can follow him about just as well."

"$catchreleaseCrabChicken_profilePrice credits and $catchreleaseCrabChicken_profileCrabs crabs. Once! You keep him."

The chicken pecks at the edge of the screen.

"No feed bill either. I've checked."

"Chicken! For the fishing display."

Crablobab puts a display tile on the counter. The chicken on it marches past a little marker.

"When your tackle doesn't show the fish, he takes its place. Doesn't identify the catch. Very good at moving about, though."

He counts what you have.

"$catchreleaseCrabChicken_profilePrice credits and $catchreleaseCrabChicken_profileCrabs crabs. You're a little short."

He draws the tile back. The chicken keeps walking.

"Come back with the rest. I'll keep him busy."

Crablobab taps the tile against your tripad, already held in his other hand. The chicken walks across.

"Installed! Try him next time you fish. If you want to put him away, the Outfitter can do it."

The chicken pecks at an app icon.

"Not that one," Crablobab tells it.

"Explosive head!"

Crablobab carries it to the counter with both hands, shoulders hunched.

"Harpoon goes in, this goes off. A very considerable improvement if you wanted an explosion."

He eases it down.

"Single use. I do like to mention that before anybody asks for it back."

The price is $catchreleaseCrabExplosive_headPrice and $catchreleaseCrabExplosive_headCrabs crabs.

"Explosive head!"

Crablobab carries it to the counter very carefully.

"Fits the harpoon. Goes off when it hits. Once. After that, come and see me again!"

He asks for $catchreleaseCrabExplosive_headPrice and $catchreleaseCrabExplosive_headCrabs crabs. You cannot cover the price.

"No explosion today." He puts it into an inside pocket. The pocket flashes once.

The head comes out of the coat wrapped, tagged, and already entered against your ship's inventory.

Your ops chief checks the timestamp.

The entry predates the sale by eleven minutes.

"A colony purchase!" Crablobab produces a blueprint chip between two fingers. "Breach Conservatory. Tanks for the public, an outfitting desk, room to do business."

He points at an elevation drawing.

"Proper glass. Children put their faces on it. Leave room for somebody to get round with a cloth."

"You learn this, you can build one on your colonies. $catchreleaseCrabConservatoryPrice and $catchreleaseCrabConservatoryCrabs crabs for the plans."

"Breach Conservatory. For your colonies!" Crablobab holds up a blueprint chip. "Public tanks, outfitting desk, proper place for the trade."

He turns it over, checking the price.

"$catchreleaseCrabConservatoryPrice and $catchreleaseCrabConservatoryCrabs crabs. Ah. Not enough today."

The chip goes into a pocket already occupied by his left hand.

"Plans don't eat. I can keep them."

The blueprint chip changes hands. Your ops chief finds it already filed under colony infrastructure, and adds the purchase receipt.

"Leave room for the visitors!" Crablobab calls after the chief. "They get bigger in groups!"

Crablobab draws a rolled backdrop from behind his knee and snaps it open against the wall.

"$catchreleaseCrabBackdropName! For the aquarium."

He steps aside to let you admire it.

"Much better than looking through the tank at whoever's standing on the other side. The fish will appreciate that too."

Crablobab snaps the backdrop open against the wall in one practiced movement. "$catchreleaseCrabBackdropName! Makes your aquarium look like an actual place. Nobody stands at a tank to look at water."

He sends a handling manifest to your bridge. "Have your deck officer look that over."

"Fish, mostly. I can show you the catch, but you won't learn much looking at it in a container. You'd do better to try a retrieval yourself."

He sends over a handling manifest. "I've a rig you can use."

"Fishing. There's a market for what comes through these ruptures, and we've been working this one."

He looks over your fleet's particulars. "Come alongside if you'd like to try it. I've a rig you can use."

"The LYNE drone carries the ROD through the rupture. The ROD takes hold, and the drone brings the catch back across."

He runs your retrieval log forward to the return. "This is where the pattern takes a shape we can handle. You'll hear spacers call what we reach for ghosts. Don't let the name do too much of your thinking for you."

text:
The Fisherman compares this retrieval with the first. He spends some time on the coherence readings before having the catch taken below.

"That's the difference I wanted you to see. The rig's done its work; the condition of the fabric still shows in what comes through."

He opens a service connection to your fleet. "You've enough experience to start choosing your own gear. I'll give you access to the outfitter."

"The outfitter has the parts and modifications for these rigs. You'll find things for the drones, the retrieval controls, the rest of the equipment as you learn to use it."

He opens the catalogue. "Have a look before you spend anything. Some of it won't be much use for the way you fish."

"Modules change how a rig works. You need the schematic before you can have one built, but once you've bought it you can fit it when you need it."

He points out the fitting controls. "You don't have to buy another every time you change your mind."

"An improvement you keep. Better performance from the machinery you already have."

He brings up the tier listing. "The early work is straightforward. For the last two tiers you'll need the appropriate schematics as well as payment."

"Ask the people who use the equipment. A working captain may have something useful and a job worth trading it for. You'll find buyers in port, too."

He brings up a schematic on his slate. "When someone offers you one of these, check what it fits before you agree to the work."
"It'll be there when you need it. Have your deck crew clear some space; there's more equipment coming over."
"Then have your deck crew clear some space. There's more equipment coming over."

The first transfer brings a bank of articulated projectors on a reinforced frame. The harpoon launcher follows, heavy enough to require both cargo booms. Your deck officer calls for another crew to help with the mounting.

"Breach Lights," the Fisherman says, indicating the projectors. "They work the fabric until we can reach a pattern without opening a full rupture. That's what the harpoon is for."

"The head carries a ROD. When you've got a return under the lights, put the harpoon into it. The ROD takes hold and the return trace brings the catch across."

He waits for your deck officer to acknowledge the installation instructions. "Mind where you aim it. The projectile is quite real."

"Not a full one. Enough to get at a pattern with the harpoon, but it isn't a passage you can send an ordinary drone through."

He brings up the local plot. "And keep the lights away from inhabited traffic."

He opens the harpoon schematic. "Your deck crew won't find a reel to service, if that's what they're looking for."

The Fisherman looks back at the installation feed. "Have your gunnery officer go over the controls with whoever's operating it. I don't want to hear you've put a harpoon through a passing freighter."
